title: Text-Driven Fusion for Infrared and Visible Images: Achieving Image Scene Adaptation on Hyperbolic Space
claim: Euclidean fusion loses semantics; a text-anchored hyperbolic process bridges the semantic gap and yields hierarchically enhanced features.
layout: 2 side-by-side process flows top, feature comparison panels bottom, large gradient arrow
description: The figure has two halves. The left half, titled Euclidean Fusion Process, shows infrared and visible source images in a dashed blue box. Arrows lead from them and from two BLIP text boxes into a single Euclidean Encoder. The output is a street image with red detection boxes and a neutral emoji, labeled Semantic Loss. The right half, titled Hyperbolic Fusion Process, shows the same source images going to BLIP text boxes, an attribute-feature icon (c, s, b, t), and an Attribute Encoder. These feed a 3D Poincaré ball with text anchors and modality points, labeled Möbius Translation. The ball feeds a Fusion Model, which outputs a similar street image with a smiley emoji, labeled Semantic Enhancement. At the bottom, two rounded boxes compare Euclidean Base Feature maps with Hierarchically Enhanced Feature maps. A large gradient red arrow reads Bridging Semantic Gap via Hyperbolic Manifold. Pastel green, teal and orange arrows carry the flow.
caption: Breaking free from the rigid geometry of Euclidean space, our text-driven hyperbolic framework bridges the modality gap. It leverages semantic anchors to hierarchically align and enhance cross-modal features, achieving a richer representation of the scene semantics.
abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion aims to integrate complementary modalities, while existing Euclidean methods impose rigid distance metrics that distort multi-modal interactions and parent-to-child semantic hierarchies. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a text-driven fusion framework empowered by hyperbolic manifold learning. During training, BLIP-extracted text prompts serve as topological anchors within the hyperbolic space, guiding vision-attribute alignment through hyperbolic embeddings that naturally accommodate varying semantic granularities. By exploiting the exponential volume growth dictated by the PoincarÃ© ball's negative curvature, this approach seamlessly embeds hierarchical trees to encode coarse-to-fine semantics without metric saturation, while the vast peripheral space prevents texture distortion during cross-modal fusion. At inference, the fusion process autonomously adapts to input content using the learned text-attribute priors, completely eliminating the need for textual input. Experimental results show our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on benchmark datasets, with code available at https://github.com/Shaoyun2023/TEDFusion.
